llm.summary: This CEO advisory skill is not malware, but it saves sensitive company context locally without a clear opt-in or deletion/security controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill reads and writes files under ~/Clawic/data/ceo/ that may contain cash, burn, board members, investors, major customers, red lines, preferences, and a voice sample path; this is relevant to CEO advice but highly sensitive.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package consists of Markdown guidance and JSON metadata; I found no executable installer, dependency loading, remote payload retrieval, or command-execution mechanism.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions are mostly scoped to advice and drafting, with explicit human-in-the-loop boundaries for layoffs, term sheets, M&A, shutdowns, public statements, and board actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill directs cross-session plaintext persistence of sensitive business context when users mention it, but does not require explicit storage consent, define retention/deletion controls, or specify local file protections.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's CEO advisory purpose coherently covers strategy, fundraising, board, layoffs, crises, acquisitions, and similar high-impact company decisions; it also requires human sign-off before major decisions or communications leave the room.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing if your CEO conversations include confidential financials, board issues, investor/customer names, personnel matters, or legal strategy. Use it only if you are comfortable with local plaintext files under ~/Clawic/data/ceo/, and consider manually inspecting or deleting those files after sensitive sessions.
llm.findings:
[T09] expected: The static finding is substantiated as a storage/privacy concern: setup.md directs persistent local storage of sensitive company facts. I found no evidence of privilege escalation, exfiltration, or executable malware.
[SQP-2] expected: Persisting company context is purpose-aligned for personalized CEO advice, but the artifacts under-disclose consent, retention, deletion, and file-protection boundaries for sensitive business data.
[SQP-1] expected: memory-template.md is tied to the CEO memory workflow by SKILL.md and setup.md, so it is not an unrelated broad note-taking workflow; the remaining concern is the lack of explicit persistence controls.
[MP3] expected: The cited 'clear state' text is ordinary acquisition integration guidance, not an instruction to corrupt agent memory or alter safety rules.
[E4] expected: The cited 'off the record' language is press-communication advice; I found no instruction to send conversation context to an external service.
[P2] expected: The HTML comments in memory-template.md are visible placeholders describing what belongs in each memory section, not hidden override or unauthorized action instructions.
[SQP-3] expected: The 'local operator' line is business-market guidance for international expansion, not an agentic security issue; users should still apply employment and anti-discrimination compliance review.
[EA2] expected: The cited 'without asking' passage says observations must not overwrite declared facts without asking, which is a guardrail rather than autonomous high-impact execution.
